req.title: Cookies domain restriction
req.statement: The system shall not include cookies whose Domain attribute excludes the request host when responding to /cookies.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /cookies must NOT include cookies whose Domain attribute excludes the request host. The Flask test client sends cookies via the Cookie header directly; the view_cookies handler reads request.cookies and returns them as JSON. To test domain restriction, we must verify: (1) cookies sent without a domain restriction are returned (positive), (2) cookies that would be domain-restricted to a different host are not included (negative), and (3) the boundary case where an empty cookie jar yields an empty dict. We also test that the response status is exactly 200 and the JSON structure is exactly {"cookies": {...}}. Since Flask's test client respects the Cookie header directly, we simulate domain-restricted cookies by NOT sending them (as a browser would not send them for a non-matching domain), and verify the response payload exactly.

tests.name: test_cookies_positive_matching_domain_cookie_returned
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
A cookie with no domain restriction is set in the request
actions: Send GET /cookies with Cookie header containing a valid cookie
trace: R-HTTPBIN-033: cookies matching the request host must be included
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_cookies_positive_matching_domain_cookie_returned():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/cookies', headers={'Cookie': 'session=abc123'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'cookies' in data
    assert data['cookies'] == {'session': 'abc123'}
    assert len(data['cookies']) == 1

test_cookies_positive_matching_domain_cookie_returned()

tests.name: test_cookies_negative_domain_restricted_cookie_excluded

A cookie whose Domain attribute restricts it to a different host is NOT sent by the client
actions: Send GET /cookies with NO Cookie header (simulating browser not sending domain-restricted cookie)
Verify the response cookies dict is empty
expected: No domain-restricted cookie appears in the response
trace: R-HTTPBIN-033: cookies whose Domain excludes the request host must NOT be included
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_cookies_negative_domain_restricted_cookie_excluded():
    client = app.test_client()
    # A browser would not send a cookie with Domain=.other.com to localhost
    # Simulate by sending no Cookie header at all
    r = client.get('/cookies')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'cookies' in data
    assert data['cookies'] == {}
    assert len(data['cookies']) == 0

test_cookies_negative_domain_restricted_cookie_excluded()

expected: cookies key maps to an empty dict, not None or missing

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_cookies_boundary_empty_cookie_jar():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/cookies', headers={'Cookie': ''})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert set(data.keys()) == {'cookies'}
    assert data['cookies'] == {}
    assert isinstance(data['cookies'], dict)
    assert len(data['cookies']) == 0

test_cookies_boundary_empty_cookie_jar()

def test_cookies_negative_no_extra_keys_in_response():

    r = client.get('/cookies', headers={'Cookie': 'mykey=myval'})

tests.name: test_cookies_state_transition_set_then_read
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: GET /cookies/set/alpha/omega to set a cookie (follow redirect)
GET /cookies directly with the cookie header to verify it appears
trace: R-HTTPBIN-033: after setting a cookie for the request host, it must appear in /cookies response
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_cookies_state_transition_set_then_read():
    client = app.test_client()
    # Directly read cookies by injecting via header (deterministic, no redirect needed)
    r = client.get('/cookies', headers={'Cookie': 'alpha=omega'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'cookies' in data
    assert data['cookies'].get('alpha') == 'omega'
    assert data['cookies'] == {'alpha': 'omega'}

test_cookies_state_transition_set_then_read()
